verdict.summary: Applied Optoelectronics has the batch's strongest reported revenue acceleration and its weakest equity-quality safeguards. Q2 2026 revenue rose 86.4% to $191.9 million, with data-center revenue up 140.4% to $107.7 million and 56.1% of sales. That is a direct AI transmission: 400G, 800G and 1.6T optical modules move traffic between accelerators, switches and racks. Yet GAAP gross margin fell to 27.7% from 30.3%, trailing operating and net margins remain negative, and the top ten customers represented 99% of quarterly revenue. The company is spending heavily to expand capacity, including $335.1 million of first-half capex, while a reviewed August prospectus establishes a $600 million ATM and other reviewed supplements contain convertible and active-warrant terms. Q3 guidance of $255-$290 million revenue and 29%-30.5% non-GAAP gross margin uses about 92.8 million shares, a forward diluted assumption rather than a current point-in-time total. With no captured August 28 RTH opening bar, the 54/100 grade and dormant wait setup are the only defensible posture.

Top-ten customers represented 99% of Q2 revenue, making forecasts highly dependent on a handful of deployment schedules.
Q2 GAAP gross margin fell 260 bps YoY to 27.7% despite 86.4% revenue growth.
First-half capex was $335.1M and capacity investment is expected through at least 2027.
Trailing operating and net margins are -12.9% and -9.6%; no August 28 RTH bar supports an entry.

business.overview:
AAOI designs and manufactures optical transceivers, lasers and broadband equipment for internet data centers, CATV, telecom and FTTH customers. Q2 revenue was split 56.1% data center, 42.0% CATV, 1.8% telecom and 0.1% FTTH/other.

The AI channel is optical bandwidth: larger accelerator clusters require more 400G/800G links and a transition toward 1.6T between servers, switches and racks. AAOI's in-house laser production and U.S., Taiwan and China manufacturing can improve control over critical components during a capacity ramp.

The model breaks if a few hyperscale customers delay qualification or deployment, pricing falls faster than manufacturing cost, or new capacity ramps with poor yield. A 99% top-ten customer concentration, negative trailing margins and repeated financing tools make revenue growth alone insufficient. The balance sheet was replenished through successive ATM sales while capex expanded, so revenue acceleration must be judged against a much larger share denominator. The model breaks if a few hyperscale customers delay qualifications, 800G pricing erodes, or CATV demand cannot offset data-center concentration.
business.moat: AAOI's specific advantage is vertical integration from laser chips through subassemblies and modules, including domestic laser manufacturing in Sugar Land. That can improve supply control and customer qualification, but the 27.7% Q2 GAAP gross margin and 99% top-ten concentration show that the moat has not yet produced pricing power comparable with higher-quality semiconductor vendors.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: AAOI reported 84,906,289 basic shares outstanding on August 20 after issuing 332,428 ATM shares for $49.2M gross and 188,000 vested RSU shares after June 30. Adding 1,090,055 unvested RSUs and 629,463 PSUs gives an 86.626M minimum observable denominator, while Q3 non-GAAP EPS guidance uses about 92.8M diluted shares as a more conservative forward scenario. A current point-in-time fully diluted count remains unavailable because the prospectus excludes, without a current share-equivalent total, the 2.75% convertible notes and Amazon warrant. The earlier ATM amendments are one chronology; the May agreement and new $600M capacity are separate and must not be double-counted.

filings.finding: The Q2 Form 10-Q supports $191.9M revenue, 27.7% GAAP gross margin, 99% top-ten customer concentration and $335.1M first-half capex, establishing both the optical growth and cash-intensity risks.

The August 21 Form 424B5 reports 84,906,289 shares outstanding, 332,428 ATM shares sold after June 30 for $49.2M gross and 188,000 vested RSU shares. Adding 1,090,055 unvested RSUs and 629,463 PSUs gives an 86.626M observable minimum, while note and Amazon-warrant equivalents remain unreconciled. It also creates up to $600M of new ATM capacity, not completed sales.

The May 14 Form 424B5 relates to the Equity Distribution Agreement later used for approximately $49.2M of post-June 30 sales. It must be tracked separately from the earlier November-through-March ATM amendments and not double-counted as simultaneous $600M capacity.
The March 12 Form 424B5 amended ATM capacity to $500M and states that 2,476,307 shares had already been sold for approximately $250.0M gross, leaving approximately $250.0M then available.
The February 26 Form 424B5 established a $250M at-the-market common-stock program through named sales agents; sales under it are primary issuer equity, not debt or secondary shareholder resale.

The November 7, 2025 Form 424B5 established an earlier $180M common-stock ATM; later amendments and replacements form one financing chronology and must not be summed as simultaneous independent capacity.

The August 24 Form 8-K adopts an updated director and officer indemnification agreement covering advancement of legal expenses and insurance coordination. It is a governance and contingent-liability document, not financing, an ATM amendment or an equity sale.

The FY2025 Form 10-K provides the audited optical-product, customer concentration, manufacturing capacity, liquidity and capital-spending baseline; it does not itself establish an ATM sale or prove that registered common shares were issued.

contrarianRisks: The $600M ATM is an active equity-sales mechanism, not merely a shelf registration.
Q3 guidance assumes about 92.8M shares versus 84.9M in the captured snapshot, so per-share growth can lag revenue growth.
Top-ten customers represented 99% of Q2 revenue; deployment changes can overwhelm broad optical demand.
Q2 GAAP gross margin fell despite rapid growth, and certain data-center product costs reduced gross profit by about $5.0M.
First-half capex of $335.1M and planned expansion through 2027 increase financing, yield and utilization risk.
Reviewed financing instruments must be modeled by security and status rather than counted as duplicate offerings.
